summary: Verified iteration 6 fix: mobile drawer rendered via ReactDOM.createPortal to document.body. All 14 test assertions passed on mobile (390x844) and desktop (1440x900). Drawer bounding rect is x=0,y=0,w=390,h=844 (full viewport), opacity=1, pointer-events=auto, aria-hidden=false when open. Drawer's parent element is BODY (portalled out of <header>). All 6 mobile links + demo button are visible and not intercepted by any overlay (elementFromPoint check). Tap on mobile-nav-link-about-us WITHOUT force navigates to /about, drawer closes cleanly (opacity=0, aria-hidden=true, body.overflow=''). X close button works. On desktop viewport, drawer is not visible.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: a console warning appears — 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative/fixed/absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly.' Not blocking, but likely originates from a scroll-tracking library (framer-motion useScroll or similar). Main agent may want to set position:relative on the scroll container to silence the warning.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 6 mobile hamburger drawer fix (createPortal to document.body) is fully verified working. Drawer height correctly = 844 on 390x844 viewport; all links clickable without force; navigation, close-on-nav, X-close, and desktop-hidden all work. Only leftover is a benign scroll-container position warning in console.
rca of the issue: Previous iteration 5 had backdrop-blur on <header> creating a containing block that made the fixed-positioned drawer collapse to height 0. Iteration 6 fix: drawer moved via ReactDOM.createPortal to document.body, escaping the header's containing-block/stacking context. Verified drawer parent is now BODY and bounding box matches viewport.
